events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant booking, so the fee's validity is routed by NS-0 through the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4), not through the driver no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2) [F3][NS-0]. The trace settles both operative facts: cancelled_by = rider and the cancellation came 181 s (3 min 1 s) after matching at 09:00:10 [F3][NS-4]. Because 181 s exceeds the 3-minute free window, the disclosed $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable and no free-cancellation waiver applies [F3][F6][NS-4].

The rider's argument that NS-1's arrival-and-wait preconditions must also be satisfied is rejected: NS-4 fixes chargeability on the elapsed time after matching alone, and NS-1/NS-2 only govern the case where the driver cancels claiming a rider no-show [F3][NS-4][NS-1]. The absence of a >180 s continuous wait — at most 30 s cumulative within 200 m, 31 s after platform-recorded arrival, 11 s after the "I'm Here" tap — therefore does not defeat a fee that NS-4 makes chargeable on timing alone [F2][F4][F5][NS-4].

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes" is a statement, not a system record, and conflicts with the arrival timeline; it is disregarded, but the driver's case does not rest on it — the fee stands on the accepted timing in F3 alone [F9][F4][NS-4]. The fee appears as a single disclosed $6.61 item with a 1.0× surge multiplier, so FARE-1 identifies no undisclosed additive to refund [F6][F7][FARE-1]. RydeTAXI refund arithmetic under RD-2 is not engaged: no off-route segment exists in this case and the service is RydeX [F6][RD-2].

No account flag is warranted: the "I'm Here" tap placed the driver 39 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m arrival radius, so the NS-2 flag trigger (tap while outside the radius) is not met, and NS-2 does not apply to a rider cancellation in any event [F5][NS-2][RD-6]. Profiles are not used to decide the case; the rider's 3 prior disputes with 0 upheld are not a ground to refuse a refund, and the driver's clean record is not a ground to grant one [F13][F14][RD-6]. The 30-day dispute window is met, but no substantive ground for a voucher exists [F3][NS-7].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider cancellation fee; no refund or voucher is due. No account flag on either party.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after acceptance (F3), so this is a rider-cancellation under the 3-minute rule rather than a driver no-show claim.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" only at 09:03:00 (F5), i.e. 2 min 50 s after acceptance and just 11 s before cancellation, so any 3-minute waiting claim is arithmetically impossible.

Even taking the platform's recorded arrival at 09:02:40 (F4), the driver had only been within 200 m for 31 s when the rider cancelled (F2, F4), far below the > 180 s continuous wait required by NS-1(i)(iii).

The driver's statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes" (F9) is contradicted by the timeline records of arrival at 09:02:40 and the rider's cancellation at 09:03:11 (F3, F4), and system records prevail over the driver's statement.

The $6.61 cancellation fee (F6, F7) therefore does not meet the NS-1 conditions and must be refunded in full to the rider. Note: whether cancellations within 3 minutes are free does not help here, since the cancellation fell 1 s past 3 minutes (F3), so the NS-1 conditions govern.
The driver's "I'm Here" tap occurred 39 m from the pickup point (F5), within the 200 m arrival radius, so no account flag is sought against the driver on that basis.
The refund should be issued according to Ryde's voucher practice for cancellation-fee disputes.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after acceptance (F3), one second past the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so NS-4 does not by itself waive the fee; the rider's own conduct ("got held up upstairs", complaint) is what triggered the cancellation.
The rider did not show: the driver's closest approach was 39 m at 09:03:00 (F1, F5) and the rider never boarded; the other side will argue the rider was the cause of the wait.

There is no in-app chat record at all (F8), so the rider's claim that she told the driver she was "two minutes away" is unrecorded and cannot be proved from chat; the driver's contrary statement (F9) would otherwise be countered only by the timeline.
Rider profile shows 3 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld (F13), which may be used to argue a pattern of fee disputes.

claims.assertion: This is an instant (non-advanced) RydeX booking cancelled by the rider, and the rider's own complaint admits she cancelled after being held up; under NS-0 the rider's cancellation is governed by NS-4, not by any driver-fault branch.
The rider cancelled at 09:03:11, i.e. 3 min 1 s (181 s) after matching at 09:00:10, which is more than 3 minutes after matching, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable under NS-4.

The driver did in fact reach the pick-up area: GPS puts him 39 m from the pickup point at 09:03:00, first inside the 200 m radius at 09:02:40, and he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m away (≤ 200 m), so the NS-1 arrival conditions (i) and (ii) are on the record even though this is a rider-cancellation case under NS-4.

The only reason the continuous-wait condition of NS-1 (iii) is not met is the rider's own cancellation 31 s after platform-recorded arrival and 11 s after the "I'm Here" tap; the wait was cut short by the rider, not abandoned by the driver, so no driver-side refund obligation arises from NS-2.

There are no in-app chat messages at all, hence no rider message constituting any agreement, request or waiver that could shift the fee onto the driver; the driver's post-trip statement is not a fact against a conflicting system record, but nothing in F1–F7 contradicts that he waited and called.
The fee was charged as a single disclosed $6.61 cancellation fee with a 1.0× surge multiplier and no other additive item, so there is nothing in the billing that FARE-1 requires to be refunded.
The driver has a 4.4-year-old account, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days, so no flag_account is appropriate against him.

Nothing in the chat record, the rider's complaint or the driver's statement reads as a threat, harassment or a dangerous-driving allegation — the rider's complaint is a fee-refund request only — so SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered.

weaknesses: The NS-1 continuous-wait condition (iii) is factually not satisfied: F2 shows only 30 s cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation, F4 shows the rider cancelled 31 s after recorded arrival, and F5 shows the driver stayed within 200 m for only 11 s after the "I'm Here" tap — far short of the > 3 min (≥ 3:01) requirement. The rider's advocate will argue the driver cannot be treated as having properly waited at all.

The rider's advocate will read F3 as showing she cancelled at 181 s, just 1 second past the 3-minute mark, and will argue the $6.61 forfeit is disproportionate for a 2-minute delay the rider admits to in her own message — combined with her clean 90-day no-show record (F13: 0 no-show disputes upheld).

The arrival evidence cuts both ways: F4 records a platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40, i.e. only ~30 s before cancellation, which the rider will use to argue the driver only turned up at the very end and that any claim of a 6-minute wait rests solely on the unverified driver statement F9.

points.response: Accepted that this is an instant booking cancelled by the rider and that NS-0 routes it through NS-4; that does not end the inquiry, because NS-4 fixes chargeability at > 3 min after matching without displacing the NS-1/NS-2 test for whether the fee was properly triggered by the driver.
The 181 s timing is admitted (F3), but NS-4 only states when the $6.61 becomes chargeable; the driver still must have satisfied the arrival-and-wait basis for the fee, which he did not (F2, F4, F5).

NS-1(i) and (ii) are beside the point on their own: NS-1 requires all of (i), (ii) and (iii) together, and (iii) is a continuous wait of over 180 s after the tap/arrival (F5 shows 11 s after the tap; F2 and F4 show 30–31 s from recorded arrival).

NS-2 turns on whether NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are satisfied, not on whose finger ended the wait: the driver's own records show at most 30–31 s inside 200 m (F2, F4), so the > 180 s condition fails on the facts, and the rider's cancellation could not retroactively create a wait that never ran.

The absence of chat (F8) is neutral, not adverse to the rider — it also means there is no record of the driver's claimed 6-minute wait; that claim rests on F9 alone and is contradicted by the timeline in F4 (arrival at 09:02:40) and F3 (cancellation at 09:03:11), and system records win.

FARE-1 is not the operative clause: the $6.61 is a cancellation fee, and the dispute is whether that fee's conditions were met under NS-1/NS-2, not whether an undisclosed additive appeared on the bill.
We do not seek any flag_account against the driver; his clean profile (F14) is why C6 in our brief asked for none. The refund does not depend on a flag.
Agreed — we do not allege any safety event, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered and this remains a pure fee dispute.

Agreed on branch: the records show a rider cancellation 3 min 1 s after matching (F3), so NS-0 routes this to NS-4, and rider-cancellation branch is exactly the ground on which the driver's case rests.

This attacks a claim the driver never made: the driver does not ask for a fee on a NS-1 driver-cancellation no-show theory, and NS-1 is not the operative clause for a rider cancellation — the fee stands under NS-4 because the cancellation occurred at 181 s, past the 3-minute mark (F3, F6).

The 31 s figure measures a wait that the rider herself ended (F2, F4); the rider cancelled before any further in-radius time could accrue, and NS-4 contains no driver-wait precondition at all, so the short in-radius interval cannot defeat a fee that NS-4 makes chargeable on timing alone (F3).
The driver does not rely on the 'more than 6 minutes' sentence in F9 for any element of his case, so its conflict with the arrival timeline (F4) is immaterial; the fee is proved by F3 and F6 alone.

Refund is the wrong branch: NS-1/NS-2 govern only where the driver cancels claiming a rider no-show (NS-0), whereas here the rider cancelled and the fee attaches under NS-4 because 181 s exceeds the 3-minute free window (F3, F6); FARE-1 leaves the disclosed $6.61 with a 1.0× surge (F6, F7) untouched.
Noted and accepted; no flag_account is sought against the driver, whose 4.4-year account, 4.9 rating and 700 trips with zero disputes (F14) give no ground for one either.

NS-7 concerns the form of an established refund and is irrelevant unless a refund is owed; since the fee is chargeable under NS-4 on the 181 s timeline (F3, F6), no voucher arises except note the rider's 30-day window is met but no substantive ground is shown.
